newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine politics not hurting cash inflows - Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Argentine politics not hurting cash inflows - Morgan.

text.p: Political spats in Argentina ahead of October mid-term elections are not stemming foreign cash flows, J.P. Morgan said Thursday.

"The important thing is that there is consensus on policy, on stability and on privatizations, although there may be political tensions in the near term," said Jose Luis Daza, J.P. Morgan's head of emerging markets research.

Speaking at a seminar at the Buenos Aires stock exchange, Daza said the Argentine political sector, shaken by corruption scandals and the murder of a journalist, had one of the most stable medium and long-term outlooks in Latin America.
He said Argentina's deep structural reforms, solid banking sector, privatizations program and regulatory framework gave it an advantage over Brazil, Mexico and Venezuela.
He also noted public debt is low as a percentage of gross domestic product at 33 percent, but remains large compared to exports, one of the main reasons Argentina's risk rating is still high.
Another reason for the perceived high country risk is that previous experiences with fixed exchange rates in Latin America have failed, Daza said.
However, he noted Argentina's case was unique because peso-dollar parity was achieved through the convertibility law, which requires every peso in circulation to be backed up by a dollar in reserves.
On the downside, he said convertibility makes Argentina dependent on exchange rate swings in the United States.

Argentina also suffers from the fear of a devaluation in Brazil, and a fiscal deficit and payments calendar which creates dependency on the capital markets. It has run up too much debt and has steep unemployment which generates political tension and undermines fiscal policy, Daza said.

He advised the government to lower the fiscal deficit, improve the tax collection system and pass laws making the labor market more flexible, this last point being "essential to have an efficient, modern economy, especially in a country with a fixed exchange rate."
